   166→                data_objects = collect_all_objects(data)

   185→def collect_all_objects(obj):

   193→    def _inner(o):

==============================================================================
UJSON (UltraJSON) - Comprehensive API and Fuzzing Target Analysis
==============================================================================

Project: ujson (UltraJSON)
Repository: https://github.com/ultrajson/ultrajson
Description: Ultra fast JSON encoder and decoder for Python, implemented as
             a C extension module.
License: BSD-3-Clause AND TCL
Python support: >=3.10 (CPython, PyPy, GraalPy)

==============================================================================
1. REPOSITORY STRUCTURE
==============================================================================

/app/ujson/
  setup.py                          -- Build configuration, C extension definition
  pyproject.toml                    -- Build system config (setuptools)
  setup.cfg                         -- Package metadata
  src/ujson/
    python/
      ujson.c                       -- Python module initialization, method table
      ujson.h                       -- Shared header (JSONDecodeError extern)
      JSONtoObj.c                   -- JSON string -> Python object (decoder)
      objToJSON.c                   -- Python object -> JSON string (encoder)
      version_template.h            -- Version string template
    lib/
      ultrajson.h                   -- Core C library header, types, structs
      ultrajsondec.c                -- Core C JSON decoder implementation
      ultrajsonenc.c                -- Core C JSON encoder implementation
    deps/
      double-conversion/            -- Third-party double<->string conversion library
  tests/
    test_ujson.py                   -- Main test suite (pytest)
    fuzz.py                         -- Existing brute-force fuzzer (encoder only)
    memory.py                       -- Memory leak detection helper
    sample.json                     -- Sample JSON file
    334-reproducer.json             -- Regression test data
  ujson-stubs/
    __init__.pyi                    -- Type stubs for the public API

==============================================================================
2. PUBLIC API (Python-level)
==============================================================================

All functions are implemented as C extension methods defined in ujson.c:

  ujson.encode(obj, ...) -> str      -- Alias: ujson.dumps()
  ujson.decode(obj) -> Any           -- Alias: ujson.loads()
  ujson.dump(obj, fp, ...) -> None   -- File-based encoder
  ujson.load(fp) -> Any              -- File-based decoder
  ujson.JSONDecodeError              -- Exception class (subclass of ValueError)
  ujson.__version__                  -- Version string

---------- ujson.encode / ujson.dumps ----------
Signature (from type stubs):
  encode(
      obj: Any,
      ensure_ascii: bool = True,
      encode_html_chars: bool = False,
      escape_forward_slashes: bool = True,
      sort_keys: bool = False,
      indent: int = 0,
      allow_nan: bool = True,
      reject_bytes: bool = True,
      default: Callable[[Any], Any] | None = None,
      separators: tuple[str, str] | None = None,
  ) -> str

C implementation: objToJSON() in src/ujson/python/objToJSON.c
  -> Calls JSON_EncodeObject() in src/ujson/lib/ultrajsonenc.c
  -> Uses double-conversion library for float formatting

---------- ujson.decode / ujson.loads ----------
Signature (from type stubs):
  decode(s: str | bytes | bytearray) -> Any
  loads(s: str | bytes | bytearray) -> Any

C implementation: JSONToObj() in src/ujson/python/JSONtoObj.c
  -> Accepts str, bytes, bytearray, or any C-contiguous buffer
  -> Calls JSON_DecodeObject() in src/ujson/lib/ultrajsondec.c
  -> Uses double-conversion library for float parsing

---------- ujson.dump ----------
Signature: dump(obj, fp, **kwargs) -> None
C implementation: objToJSONFile() in src/ujson/python/objToJSON.c
  -> Calls objToJSON() internally, then writes result to fp.write()

---------- ujson.load ----------
Signature: load(fp) -> Any
C implementation: JSONFileToObj() in src/ujson/python/JSONtoObj.c
  -> Calls fp.read(), then passes result to JSONToObj()

==============================================================================
3. C EXTENSION INTERNALS (Key Functions)
==============================================================================

--- Decoder (ultrajsondec.c) ---
  JSON_DecodeObject(dec, buffer, cbBuffer)    -- Entry point for decoding
  decode_any(ds)                              -- Top-level dispatch (string/number/etc.)
  decode_string(ds)                           -- String parsing with UTF-8 and \uXXXX
  decode_numeric(ds)                          -- Number parsing (int/long/double/NaN/Inf)
  decodeDouble(ds)                            -- Floating point via dconv_s2d()
  decode_array(ds)                            -- Array parsing with depth tracking
  decode_object(ds)                           -- Object parsing with depth tracking
  decode_true/decode_false/decode_null(ds)    -- Literal keyword parsing

--- Encoder (ultrajsonenc.c) ---
  JSON_EncodeObject(obj, enc, buffer, cbBuffer, outLen) -- Entry point for encoding
  encode(obj, enc, name, cbName)              -- Recursive encoder
  Buffer_EscapeStringValidated(obj, enc, io, end) -- UTF-8 validated string escaping
  Buffer_EscapeStringUnvalidated(enc, io, end)    -- Raw string escaping
  Buffer_Realloc(enc, cbNeeded)               -- Dynamic buffer management
  Buffer_AppendDoubleDconv(obj, enc, value)   -- Float formatting via dconv_d2s()
  Buffer_AppendLongUnchecked(enc, value)      -- Integer formatting
  Buffer_AppendUnsignedLongUnchecked(enc, value) -- Unsigned integer formatting

--- Python<->C Bridge (JSONtoObj.c) ---
  JSONToObj(self, args, kwargs)               -- Python entry: parses args, calls decoder
  JSONFileToObj(self, args, kwargs)           -- Python entry: reads file, calls JSONToObj
  Object_newString(prv, start, end)           -- Creates Python str from decoded chars
  Object_newInteger/Long/UnsignedLong(prv, value) -- Creates Python int
  Object_newDouble(prv, value)                -- Creates Python float
  Object_newIntegerFromString(prv, value, length) -- Creates Python int from string
  Object_objectAddKey(prv, obj, name, value)  -- Adds key-value to Python dict
  Object_arrayAddItem(prv, obj, value)        -- Appends item to Python list

--- Python<->C Bridge (objToJSON.c) ---
  objToJSON(self, args, kwargs)               -- Python entry: parses args, calls encoder
  objToJSONFile(self, args, kwargs)           -- Python entry: encodes then writes to file
  Object_beginTypeContext(obj, tc, enc)       -- Type dispatch for encoding
  Dict_iterNext/SortedDict_iterNext           -- Dictionary iteration
  Dict_convertKey(key)                        -- Converts dict keys to strings
  PyUnicodeToUTF8Raw(obj, outLen, pBytesObj)  -- Unicode to UTF-8 conversion

==============================================================================
4. SECURITY-RELEVANT BOUNDARIES AND ATTACK SURFACE
==============================================================================

4.1 Input Parsing (HIGHEST PRIORITY for fuzzing)
  - decode_string(): Handles UTF-8 multi-byte sequences, \uXXXX escapes,
    surrogate pairs. Manual pointer arithmetic on raw bytes. Buffer
    reallocation for escape sequences. This is the most complex and
    error-prone decoder component.
  - decode_numeric(): Handles sign, integer overflow detection, transitions
    to float parsing. Uses custom overflow detection logic.
  - decodeDouble(): Delegates to dconv_s2d() from the double-conversion
    library. Length clamped to INT_MAX to prevent integer overflow.
  - decode_array()/decode_object(): Depth tracking (JSON_MAX_OBJECT_DEPTH=1024),
    recursive descent. Memory management for intermediate Python objects.

4.2 Buffer Management
  - ultrajsondec.c uses a stack-allocated escape buffer (escBuffer) of
    JSON_MAX_STACK_BUFFER_SIZE (1024) bytes, with heap fallback via realloc.
    SIZE_MAX overflow checks present.
  - ultrajsonenc.c uses a caller-provided 65536-byte stack buffer with
    heap fallback via Buffer_Realloc(). Doubling strategy in non-debug mode.

4.3 UTF-8 Validation
  - Decoder validates UTF-8 sequences (overlong detection, continuation
    byte checks) but there are edge cases around truncated sequences.
  - Encoder has both validated (forceASCII=true) and unvalidated paths.
  - Surrogate pair handling in both encode and decode is complex.

4.4 Integer Boundaries
  - JSINT32, JSINT64, JSUINT64 type transitions during numeric parsing.
  - Overflow to string-based integer representation for very large numbers.
  - Encoder handles INT64_MIN special case.

4.5 Object/Array Depth
  - Max recursion depth: 1024 for both encoder and decoder.
  - Encoder has separate recursion tracking (enc->level vs enc->recursionMax).

==============================================================================
5. EXISTING TEST COVERAGE ANALYSIS
==============================================================================

The existing test suite (tests/test_ujson.py) covers:
  - Basic encode/decode round-trips for all JSON types
  - Unicode encoding (BMP, symbols, surrogate pairs, 4-byte UTF-8)
  - Numeric edge cases (large ints, special longs, doubles, NaN/Inf)
  - Error handling (malformed JSON, broken arrays/objects/strings)
  - Recursion depth limits
  - File I/O (dump/load)
  - Special keys (None, True, False as dict keys)
  - sort_keys option
  - indent option (including huge indents)
  - separators option
  - reject_bytes option
  - default function
  - toDict() and __json__() protocols
  - Ref counting correctness
  - Memory leak detection
  - Bytes-like input (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)

The existing fuzzer (tests/fuzz.py) only fuzzes ujson.dumps() with random
Python objects, checking for crashes and ref count leaks. It does NOT fuzz
ujson.loads() with arbitrary byte strings.

GAPS IN EXISTING TESTING (fuzzing opportunities):
  - No systematic fuzzing of ujson.loads() with arbitrary/malformed input
  - No fuzzing of ujson.loads() with bytes input (vs string)
  - No fuzzing of the decode->encode round-trip
  - No fuzzing with vary large inputs or deeply nested structures
  - No systematic testing of all encoder option combinations with adversarial input
  - Limited coverage of edge cases in numeric parsing (e.g., numbers near
    INT64_MIN/MAX boundary, numbers with many digits)
  - Limited coverage of malformed UTF-8 sequences in bytes input
  - No fuzzing of the encode path with adversarial default functions

==============================================================================
6. RECOMMENDED FUZZING TARGETS (Ranked by Security Value)
==============================================================================

PRIORITY 1 (Critical - untrusted input parsing via C extensions):

  Target: ujson.loads() / ujson.decode()
  Why: Parses untrusted input (str or bytes) through C extension code.
       Complex state machine handles UTF-8, unicode escapes, numeric parsing,
       nested structures. Highest risk for memory corruption, buffer overflows,
       integer overflows, and crashes.
  Input types: str, bytes, bytearray
  Key C functions exercised:
    - JSON_DecodeObject() -> decode_any() -> decode_string(), decode_numeric(),
      decode_array(), decode_object()
  Specific sub-targets to focus on:
    a) Malformed UTF-8 byte sequences
    b) Unicode escape sequences (\uXXXX, surrogate pairs)
    c) Extremely large/small numbers near integer boundaries
    d) Deeply nested arrays/objects
    e) Strings with embedded null bytes
    f) Truncated input at various points

PRIORITY 2 (High - encoding with adversarial objects):

  Target: ujson.dumps() / ujson.encode()
  Why: While encoding typically receives trusted data, adversarial objects
       can trigger edge cases in the C encoder. The encode path has complex
       buffer management and string escaping logic.
  Input types: dict, list, str, int, float, custom objects
  Key scenarios:
    a) Very long strings with special characters
    b) Deeply nested structures
    c) Various option combinations (ensure_ascii, encode_html_chars,

    d) Custom objects with toDict()/__json__() returning unexpected types

PRIORITY 3 (Medium - round-trip fuzzing):

  Target: ujson.loads(ujson.dumps(obj)) round-trip
  Why: Ensures encode-decode consistency and catches edge cases where

PRIORITY 4 (Lower - file-based operations):

  Target: ujson.load() / ujson.dump()
  Why: Thin wrappers around loads/dumps, but exercise the file protocol

Here is a summary of the analysis performed and the files produced.

## Analysis Summary

### Repository Overview

ujson (UltraJSON) is an ultra-fast JSON encoder/decoder for Python implemented as a C extension module. The codebase consists of:

- **Python C extension bridge** (`/app/ujson/src/ujson/python/`): `ujson.c` (module init), `JSONtoObj.c` (decoder bridge), `objToJSON.c` (encoder bridge)
- **Core C library** (`/app/ujson/src/ujson/lib/`): `ultrajsondec.c` (decoder), `ultrajsonenc.c` (encoder), `ultrajson.h` (types/structs)
- **Third-party dependency** (`/app/ujson/src/ujson/deps/double-conversion/`): double-to-string and string-to-double conversion
- **Tests** (`/app/ujson/tests/`): `test_ujson.py` (main test suite), `fuzz.py` (existing encoder-only brute-force fuzzer)

### Public API

The module exposes 6 functions and 1 exception:
- `ujson.encode()` / `ujson.dumps()` -- encode Python objects to JSON strings
- `ujson.decode()` / `ujson.loads()` -- decode JSON strings/bytes to Python objects
- `ujson.dump()` / `ujson.load()` -- file-based variants
- `ujson.JSONDecodeError` -- exception class (subclass of `ValueError`)

### Key Fuzzing Targets Identified

1. **`ujson.loads()` with string input** -- The highest-priority target. Parses untrusted input through the C decoder (`ultrajsondec.c`) which has complex manual pointer arithmetic for UTF-8 handling, unicode escape sequences (`\uXXXX` with surrogate pair logic), numeric overflow detection, and recursive array/object parsing with depth limits.

2. **`ujson.loads()` with bytes input** -- Exercises the buffer protocol path, allowing malformed UTF-8 sequences to reach the C decoder without Python's built-in unicode validation.

3. **`ujson.dumps()` with various inputs** -- Exercises the encoder's buffer management (`Buffer_Realloc`), string escaping (both validated and unvalidated UTF-8 paths), and recursive object traversal.

4. **`ujson.dumps()` with option combinations** -- Different options (`ensure_ascii`, `encode_html_chars`, `indent`, `sort_keys`, `separators`) activate different code paths in the encoder.

5. **Round-trip (`loads` then `dumps`)** -- Catches inconsistencies between encoder output and decoder expectations.

### Existing Coverage Gaps

The existing test suite has good coverage of basic functionality but the existing fuzzer (`tests/fuzz.py`) only fuzzes `ujson.dumps()` with random Python objects. There is **no systematic fuzzing of `ujson.loads()` with arbitrary/malformed byte strings**, which is the most security-critical gap given that `loads()` is the primary function processing untrusted external input.

### Output Files

- **`/app/ujson/APIs.txt`** -- Comprehensive analysis (7 sections) covering repository structure, public API, C extension internals, security-relevant boundaries, existing test coverage, recommended fuzzing targets ranked by priority, and key files for harness development.

- **`/app/ujson/notes_for_testing.txt`** -- Concise listing of the top 5 fuzzing targets with function name, file path, import statement, rationale, input type, and example usage for each.
